settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: findNull() returning -1 is explicitly handled with an ImageReadException, so unterminated names are rejected.
PngChunkIccp is only constructed when chunkType equals ChunkType.iCCP.value, so unrelated PNGs are unaffected.
The failure is limited to unchecked exceptions in the parser (DoS/robustness); no memory-safety or code-execution primitive is demonstrated.
candidates.description: In PngChunkIccp's constructor the profile name terminator index is located with findNull(bytes). Only the absence of a null terminator (index < 0) is rejected. The code then reads compressionMethod = bytes[index + 1] and computes compressedProfileLength = bytes.length - (index + 1 + 1) and allocates/System.arraycopy's using that length. Neither step verifies that at least two bytes follow the name terminator. A PNG whose iCCP chunk data is a name followed immediately by the terminating NUL at the very end of the chunk (index == bytes.length - 1) makes bytes[index + 1] throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; an empty chunk or a chunk of length 1 containing only 0x00 similarly produces index+1 out of range and a negative compressedProfileLength (NegativeArraySizeException). These exceptions escape as unchecked RuntimeExceptions. Reachability path: readChunks() dispatches to new PngChunkIccp(...) for chunkType == ChunkType.iCCP.value (PngImageParser lines 179-180), and getICCProfileBytes() calls readChunks() requesting iCCP chunks. The chunk byte array is the raw chunk data read by readBytes for the declared chunk length, so a small crafted chunk reaches this constructor directly. Impact is a denial-of-service / robustness failure (crash on malformed input) rather than memory corruption. This is a candidate: only the constructor and PngImageParser's dispatch/read loop were read; readBytes' behavior on short/EOF data and any additional validation in the chunk base class were not inspected.
missing_evidence: readBytes/skipBytes behavior in BinaryFunctions for chunk lengths that exceed or meet the remaining stream (does it pre-validate?), not in the allowed spans.
Wrapping of parser exceptions by Imaging.getICCProfileBytes / higher-level callers was not read.
PngChunk base class constructor contents (whether it re-validates bytes vs length) were not read.
preconditions: Application parses an untrusted PNG and requests the ICC profile (or otherwise causes the iCCP chunk to be constructed).
Attacker supplies an iCCP chunk whose data consists of a profile name terminated by a NUL that is the final byte of the chunk, or a 0/1-byte chunk.
candidates.title: PngChunkIccp parses attacker-controlled iCCP chunk without validating compression-method byte, allowing AIOOBE / NegativeArraySizeException

counter_evidence: findNull(...) occurrences returning < 0 are converted into ImageReadException, so missing NUL terminators are handled.
PngChunkZtxt validates that compressionMethod equals COMPRESSION_DEFLATE_INFLATE before inflating.
PngChunkItxt validates the compression flag range and the compression method when compressed.
candidates.description: PngChunkItxt computes keyword/languageTag/translatedKeyword using findNull and then increments the index repeatedly. After the keyword terminator it executes compressionFlag = bytes[index++] and compressionMethod = bytes[index++], and later reads terminator = findNull(bytes, index). PngChunkZtxt similarly does index = findNull(bytes) then index++, compressionMethod = bytes[index++]. There is no check that index remains within bytes.length after the increment. A crafted iTXt/zTXt chunk in which the keyword's NUL terminator is the last byte (or where the language-tag/translated-keyword terminators fall at the buffer end) causes bytes[index] to be read out of bounds, resulting in an uncaught ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. If findNull(bytes, index) is called with index == bytes.length, the helper's own bounds behavior becomes the deciding factor. Reachable through readChunks(): chunkType == ChunkType.iTXt.value constructs PngChunkItxt (line 197-198) and chunkType == ChunkType.zTXt.value constructs PngChunkZtxt (line 183-184), with bytes being the raw chunk data. Impact is denial-of-service on malformed input. Candidate only: the chunk dispatch and constructors were read, but helper implementations and caller-level exception handling were not fully examined.
missing_evidence: findNull(byte[], int) implementation (whether it guards against start index >= length) is in BinaryFunctions, not in the allowed spans.
Whether readBytes guarantees bytes.length == requested chunk length for truncated streams was not read.
preconditions: Application parses an untrusted PNG containing iTXt or zTXt chunks.
Attacker crafts a chunk where a required terminator/field would be read at or beyond the end of the chunk data.
candidates.title: PngChunkItxt / PngChunkZtxt read fields past parsed terminator indexes without bounds validation on crafted chunks

counter_evidence: The method does throw ImageReadException ("Unpack bits source exhausted") when i >= bytes.length at the start of an iteration, so complete exhaustion before a new control byte is handled.
Byte values of -128 are explicitly rejected with ImageReadException.
Writes go to a ByteArrayOutputStream, so output growth is bounded by input length rather than unbounded allocation.
candidates.description: PackBits.decompress loops while (total < expected). It checks i >= bytes.length only once at the top of each iteration. In the literal branch (0 <= n <= 127) it enters a loop writing bytes[i++] count = n+1 times without re-checking i < bytes.length; in the run branch it reads b = bytes[i++] also without a bound check. If the remaining source bytes are fewer than the run/literal count, i exceeds bytes.length and bytes[i++] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (uncaught RuntimeException). Because this class is used for TIFF/other PackBits-compressed data, a truncated or maliciously crafted PackBits stream can trigger the failure. Note the outer total counter can also overshoot the expected/pixelsPerStrip value, causing more output than requested. Candidate only: the class was read, but callers that supply bytes and expected (e.g. TIFF strip decompression) were not traced in the allowed spans.
missing_evidence: Callers of PackBits.decompress (which formats/compression codes reach it, and whether they pre-validate the compressed length) were not read.
Whether the surrounding TIFF reader catches RuntimeException and converts it to ImageReadException was not verified.
preconditions: Application decompresses PackBits data from an untrusted source.
Attacker supplies a run/literal control byte whose declared count exceeds the remaining bytes in the buffer.
candidates.title: PackBits.decompress advances index i without re-bounding inside literal/run loops, allowing out-of-bounds read on truncated source

counter_evidence: nRows is clamped so that y + nRows does not exceed yLimit, limiting rows processed.
The 8/24-bit fast paths require isHomogenous(8) and predictor != 2, narrowing the applicable cases.
An out-of-bounds index produces a runtime exception (crash) rather than silent memory corruption.
candidates.description: In DataReaderStrips.interpretStrip, the fast paths compute nRows = pixelsPerStrip / width (clamped to yLimit - y) and then iterate rows (i0..i1) x width, reading bytes[k++] (& the RGB path further reads bytes[k+1], bytes[k+2]) with no check that k stays below bytes.length. width, height and pixelsPerStrip derive from TIFF header/directory fields and from the strip data length. A crafted TIFF whose declared width/rows-per-strip make the computed pixel count exceed the actual decompressed strip byte array would drive k past bytes.length, producing an uncaught ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Note also bytes[k] in the RGB path is sign-extended (no & 0xff) while bytes[k+1]/bytes[k+2] are masked, an inconsistency in the same expression. This is a candidate robustness/OOB-read issue on malformed input; only lines 1-200 of this class were read (the strip-length/rows-per-strip setup in readImageData from line 199 onward and the caller in ImageDataReader were not fully examined), so the existence of upstream validation cannot be confirmed.
missing_evidence: The remainder of readImageData (lines 200+) that computes pixelsPerStrip/rowsPerStrip and obtains strip bytes was not read (tool call on that range was rejected).
Whether TiffImageData.Strips / ImageDataReader validate strip byte counts against expected dimensions before calling interpretStrip was not inspected.
preconditions: Application decodes an untrusted TIFF using the strip reader with bitsPerPixel 8 or 24 and all samples one byte.
Header width/rows-per-strip (or strip byte counts) are crafted so the expected pixel loop reads past the provided strip buffer.
candidates.title: DataReaderStrips optimized 8bpp/24bpp paths index bytes[] using header-derived dimensions without visible bounds check
